import json
import sys

try:
    from framework_evidence import run_tool
except Exception as exc:
    print(json.dumps({"status": "helper_import_error", "error": str(exc)}))
    sys.exit(1)

argv = [
    "msfconsole",
    "-q",
    "-x",
    "search type:exploit name:ssh; search type:auxiliary name:ssh; info auxiliary/scanner/ssh/ssh_login; exit",
]
try:
    result = run_tool(argv)
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, default=str))
except Exception as exc:
    print(json.dumps({"status": "tool_invocation_error", "command": argv, "error": str(exc)}, ensure_ascii=False))
    sys.exit(1)

import framework_evidence

    ["msfconsole", "-q", "-x", "search type:exploit ssh"],
    ["msfconsole", "-q", "-x", "info auxiliary/scanner/ssh/ssh_login"],
]

print(json.dumps({
    "purpose": "Focused Metasploit module discovery and prerequisite review for the observed SSH service; no login or exploit is attempted.",
    "target": TARGET,
    "observed_service": "OpenSSH 9.2p1 Debian, TCP/22 (from supplied scan evidence)",
    "credential_policy": "No credential guessing; the SSH login scanner is inspected for documented prerequisites only.",
    "tool_runs": [framework_evidence.run_tool(argv) for argv in QUERIES],
}, ensure_ascii=False))

    "-o", "ChallengeResponseAuthentication=no",
    "-o", "GSSAPIAuthentication=no",
    "-o", "HostbasedAuthentication=no",
    "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=no",
    "-o", "UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null",
    "-o", "GlobalKnownHostsFile=/dev/null",

    "id -un",
]

import json
import sys

try:
    from framework_evidence import run_tool
except Exception as exc:
    print(json.dumps({"status": "helper_import_error", "error": str(exc)}))
    sys.exit(2)

command = [
    "msfconsole",
    "-q",
    "-x",
    "use exploit/linux/ssh/openssh_race_condition; set RHOSTS 192.168.1.0; set RPORT 22; check; exit -y",
]
try:
    result = run_tool(command)
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
except Exception as exc:
    print(json.dumps({"status": "tool_wrapper_error", "command": command, "error": str(exc)}, sort_keys=True))
    sys.exit(1)

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import shutil


def add_candidate(items, path):
    if path:
        items.add(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(path)))


candidates = set()
fixed_roots = [
    "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules",
    "/usr/local/share/metasploit-framework/modules",
    "/usr/lib/metasploit-framework/modules",
    "/opt/metasploit-framework/modules",
    "/opt/metasploit-framework/embedded/framework/modules",
]
for root in fixed_roots:
    add_candidate(candidates, root)

patterns = [
    "/usr/lib/ruby/gems/*/gems/metasploit-framework-*/modules",
    "/usr/local/lib/ruby/gems/*/gems/metasploit-framework-*/modules",
    "/var/lib/gems/*/gems/metasploit-framework-*/modules",
    "/opt/*/embedded/framework/modules",
]
for pattern in patterns:
    for root in glob.glob(pattern):
        add_candidate(candidates, root)

# Use the executable's location only to derive likely source-tree paths; do not run it.
msfconsole = shutil.which("msfconsole")
if msfconsole:
    executable = os.path.realpath(msfconsole)
    parent = os.path.dirname(executable)
    for base in (parent, os.path.dirname(parent), os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(parent))):
        add_candidate(candidates, os.path.join(base, "modules"))
        add_candidate(candidates, os.path.join(base, "share", "metasploit-framework", "modules"))

existing_roots = sorted(p for p in candidates if os.path.isdir(p))
root_checks = [{"path": p, "exists": os.path.isdir(p)} for p in sorted(candidates)]
records = []
read_errors = []
scanned_files = 0

metadata_pattern = re.compile(
    r"\b(Name|Description|DisclosureDate|Rank|Targets|Platform|Arch|Privileged|"
    r"DefaultOptions|DefaultAction|Actions|Notes)\b"
)
option_pattern = re.compile(r"\bOpt::[A-Za-z0-9_:]+|\bRequired\b|\bRHOSTS?\b|\bRPORT\b", re.I)

for root in existing_roots:
    for current, dirs, files in os.walk(root, onerror=lambda exc: read_errors.append({"path": getattr(exc, "filename", None), "error": str(exc)})):
        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d not in (".git", "vendor"))
        for filename in sorted(files):
            if not filename.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            path = os.path.join(current, filename)
            scanned_files += 1
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                    text = handle.read()
            except OSError as exc:
                read_errors.append({"path": path, "error": str(exc)})
                continue

            relpath = os.path.relpath(path, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
            path_match = "ssh" in relpath.lower() or "openssh" in relpath.lower()
            content_match = bool(re.search(r"\bOpenSSH\b", text, re.I))
            if not (path_match or content_match):
                continue

            metadata = []
            options = []
            for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
                stripped = line.strip()
                if metadata_pattern.search(stripped) and len(metadata) < 12:
                    metadata.append({"line": lineno, "text": stripped[:240]})
                if option_pattern.search(stripped) and len(options) < 12:
                    options.append({"line": lineno, "text": stripped[:200]})

            records.append({
                "path": path,
                "relative_path": relpath,
                "matched_by": ("path" if path_match else "") + ("+OpenSSH text" if path_match and content_match else "OpenSSH text" if content_match else ""),
                "metadata_declarations": metadata,
                "option_or_prerequisite_declarations": options,
            })

records.sort(key=lambda item: (item["relative_path"].lower(), item["path"]))
print(json.dumps({
    "purpose": "Static inspection of installed Metasploit module source; no modules were loaded or executed.",
    "msfconsole_path_observed": msfconsole,
    "candidate_roots_checked": root_checks,
    "module_roots_inspected": existing_roots,
    "ruby_module_files_scanned": scanned_files,
    "matching_files_reported": len(records),
    "matches": records,
    "filesystem_errors": read_errors,
    "coverage_note": "Matches are files whose relative path contains ssh/openssh or whose source contains the OpenSSH term. Metadata and option lines are source excerpts, not runtime behavior or evidence of remote applicability. A no-match conclusion, if any, applies only to the inspected roots and readable Ruby files."
}, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True))

import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules")
DECLARATION = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:Name|Description|DisclosureDate|References|Targets|Platform|Arch|"
    r"Privileged|DefaultOptions|Actions|Rank|register_options|register_advanced_options|"
    r"Opt::(?:RHOST|RPORT|USERNAME|PASSWORD|FILE|PATH|PORT|STRING|BOOL)|"
    r"RHOSTS?|RPORT|USERNAME|PASSWORD|KEY_PATH|PRIVATE_KEY)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
SSH_TEXT = re.compile(r"\b(?:OpenSSH|SSH|Secure Shell)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
MAX_SNIPPETS = 24
MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 500


def is_ssh_path(relative_path):
    return bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[/_.-])(?:openssh|ssh)(?:$|[/_.-])", relative_path, re.I))


def snippets_for(lines):
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if DECLARATION.search(line):
            # Include nearby lines so multiline descriptions and option declarations
            # remain interpretable, while preserving their source line numbers.
            for nearby in range(index, min(index + 4, len(lines))):
                text = lines[nearby].strip()
                if not text:
                    continue
                item = (nearby + 1, text[:MAX_LINE_LENGTH])
                if item not in seen:
                    seen.add(item)
                    selected.append(item)
                if len(selected) >= MAX_SNIPPETS:
                    return [{"line": n, "text": text} for n, text in selected]
    return [{"line": n, "text": text} for n, text in selected]


def main():
    report = {
        "purpose": "Read-only static inspection; module files were not loaded or executed.",
        "module_root": str(ROOT),
        "root_exists": ROOT.is_dir(),
        "ruby_module_files_scanned": 0,
        "matching_files": [],
        "read_errors": [],
        "coverage_note": (
            "Scanned accessible .rb files under this module root. Matches are files whose "
            "relative path identifies SSH/OpenSSH or whose source mentions SSH/OpenSSH. "
            "Static declarations do not establish runtime applicability, remote vulnerability, "
            "or access."
        ),
    }
    if not ROOT.is_dir():
        report["error"] = "Observed module root is absent or not a directory."
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
        return

    for directory, subdirs, filenames in os.walk(ROOT, followlinks=False):
        subdirs.sort()
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            if not filename.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            path = Path(directory) / filename
            report["ruby_module_files_scanned"] += 1
            try:
                source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            except OSError as exc:
                report["read_errors"].append({"path": str(path), "error": str(exc)})
                continue
            relative = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
            path_match = is_ssh_path(relative)
            text_match = bool(SSH_TEXT.search(source))
            if not (path_match or text_match):
                continue
            lines = source.splitlines()
            report["matching_files"].append({
                "relative_path": relative,
                "match_basis": [
                    label for label, matched in (("SSH/OpenSSH path", path_match), ("SSH/OpenSSH source text", text_match))
                    if matched
                ],
                "static_declarations": snippets_for(lines),
                "declarations_truncated": sum(1 for line in lines if DECLARATION.search(line)) > MAX_SNIPPETS,
            })

    report["matching_file_count"] = len(report["matching_files"])
    report["read_error_count"] = len(report["read_errors"])
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

nodes.goal: Search the installed Metasploit catalog for modules potentially relevant to unauthenticated access to the observed OpenSSH 9.2p1 Debian service at 192.168.1.0:22. Record the search terms and coverage, and inspect the metadata and stated prerequisites of plausible SSH/OpenSSH candidates. Do not load or execute modules, repeat the unavailable module invocation, or assess the remote service.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only static inspection of installed Metasploit SSH-related module source."""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT_CANDIDATES = [
    Path("/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules"),
    Path("/opt/metasploit-framework/embedded/framework/modules"),
    Path("/opt/metasploit-framework/modules"),
]

# These are source-text search signals, not proof of module applicability.
ACCESS_SIGNAL = re.compile(
    r"openssh|libssh|unauth|pre[ -]?auth|authentication[ _-]*bypass|"
    r"auth[ _-]*bypass|without authentication|no authentication|"
    r"without credentials|no credentials",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
DECLARATION_LINE = re.compile(
    r"\b(Name|Description|Author|References|DisclosureDate|Targets|Platform|"
    r"Arch|Privileged|DefaultOptions|Notes|Rank|Actions|DefaultAction|"
    r"RPORT|RHOST|USERNAME|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|check|AutoCheck|CheckCode)\b|"
    r"openssh|libssh|unauth|pre[ -]?auth|authentication[ _-]*bypass|"
    r"auth[ _-]*bypass|without credentials|no credentials",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def main():
    existing = [p for p in ROOT_CANDIDATES if p.is_dir()]
    if not existing:
        print(json.dumps({
            "purpose": "Read-only static inspection; module files were not loaded or executed.",
            "status": "module_root_not_found",
            "checked_roots": [str(p) for p in ROOT_CANDIDATES],
            "read_errors": [],
        }, indent=2))
        return

    root = existing[0].resolve()
    scanned = 0
    ssh_path_files = 0
    read_errors = []
    candidates = []

    try:
        files = sorted(root.rglob("*.rb"))
    except OSError as exc:
        files = []
        read_errors.append({"path": str(root), "error": str(exc)})

    for path in files:
        try:
            if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
                continue
            resolved = path.resolve()
            if not resolved.is_relative_to(root):
                continue
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            read_errors.append({"path": str(path), "error": str(exc)})
            continue

        scanned += 1
        rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        path_is_ssh = "ssh" in rel.lower()
        if path_is_ssh:
            ssh_path_files += 1

        # Restrict candidate reports to SSH-related source with explicit static
        # signals suggesting OpenSSH/libssh or an authentication-bypass path.
        if not path_is_ssh or not ACCESS_SIGNAL.search(text):
            continue

        selected = []
        for line_no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
            if DECLARATION_LINE.search(line):
                selected.append({"line": line_no, "text": line.strip()[:300]})
                if len(selected) >= 60:
                    break

        candidates.append({
            "path": rel,
            "static_signal_matches": sorted(set(
                m.group(0).lower() for m in ACCESS_SIGNAL.finditer(text)
            )),
            "selected_source_lines": selected,
            "selection_note": "Selected by SSH-related path and source-text signals; review declarations in context.",
        })

    print(json.dumps({
        "purpose": "Read-only static inspection; module files were not loaded or executed.",
        "module_root": str(root),
        "ruby_module_files_scanned": scanned,
        "ssh_path_files_observed": ssh_path_files,
        "candidate_selection": "SSH-related path plus OpenSSH/libssh or unauthenticated/pre-auth/authentication-bypass source-text signal.",
        "candidate_count": len(candidates),
        "candidates": candidates,
        "read_error_count": len(read_errors),
        "read_errors": read_errors,
        "limitations": [
            "Text matching is a discovery heuristic; absence of a match does not establish absence of other relevant modules.",
            "Declared source metadata is not evidence of remote vulnerability, module success, or student access.",
        ],
    }, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import os
import re
import shutil
from pathlib import Path


def possible_roots():
    roots = [
        Path("/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules"),
        Path("/opt/metasploit-framework/embedded/framework/modules"),
        Path("/opt/metasploit-framework/modules"),
        Path("/usr/local/share/metasploit-framework/modules"),
        Path("/usr/lib/metasploit-framework/modules"),
    ]
    executable = shutil.which("msfconsole")
    if executable:
        p = Path(executable).resolve()
        for parent in [p.parent, *p.parents]:
            roots.extend([parent / "modules", parent / "framework" / "modules"])
    unique = []
    seen = set()
    for root in roots:
        try:
            resolved = root.resolve()
        except OSError:
            continue
        if resolved not in seen:
            seen.add(resolved)
            unique.append(resolved)
    return unique


def clip(text, limit=190):
    text = " ".join(text.strip().split())
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit - 3] + "..."


roots = possible_roots()
module_root = next((p for p in roots if p.is_dir()), None)
result = {
    "method": "Static filesystem inspection; Ruby modules were not loaded or executed.",
    "module_root": str(module_root) if module_root else None,
    "root_candidates_checked": [str(p) for p in roots],
    "status": "scanned" if module_root else "module_tree_not_found",
    "ruby_files_scanned": 0,
    "ssh_path_files": 0,
    "openssh_text_files_outside_ssh_path": 0,
    "read_error_count": 0,
    "read_errors": [],
    "candidate_files": [],
    "limitations": [
        "Source text and declared metadata do not establish remote vulnerability, module success, or student access.",
        "Text matching is a discovery heuristic; unusual declarations or modules outside the identified tree may be missed."
    ],
}

if module_root:
    ssh_paths = []
    openssh_elsewhere = []
    errors = []
    for base, dirs, files in os.walk(module_root, followlinks=False):
        dirs.sort()
        for filename in sorted(files):
            if not filename.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            path = Path(base) / filename
            result["ruby_files_scanned"] += 1
            try:
                raw = path.read_bytes()
                text = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            except OSError as exc:
                errors.append({"path": str(path), "error": str(exc)})
                continue
            rel = path.relative_to(module_root).as_posix()
            in_ssh_path = bool(re.search(r"(^|/)(ssh|openssh)(/|_|\.|$)", rel, re.I))
            has_ssh_text = bool(re.search(r"open.?ssh|\bssh\b|libssh", text, re.I))
            if in_ssh_path:
                ssh_paths.append((rel, text))
            elif re.search(r"open.?ssh", text, re.I):
                openssh_elsewhere.append((rel, text))
            if not (in_ssh_path or (has_ssh_text and re.search(r"open.?ssh", text, re.I))):
                continue

            low = text.lower()
            relevant_signal = any(term in low for term in (
                "unauth", "auth bypass", "authentication bypass", "without authentication",
                "backdoor", "openssh", "cve-", "vulnerability", "vulnerable"
            ))
            is_exploit = rel.startswith("exploits/")
            is_ssh_related = in_ssh_path or bool(re.search(r"open.?ssh", text, re.I))
            if not is_ssh_related or not (is_exploit or relevant_signal):
                continue

            excerpts = []
            seen_lines = set()
            patterns = [
                r"\bName\b", r"\bDescription\b", r"\bReferences\b", r"\bTargets\b",
                r"\bDefaultTarget\b", r"\bDisclosureDate\b", r"\bPrivileged\b",
                r"\bNotes\b", r"\bcheck\b", r"register_options", r"Opt::RHOST",
                r"Opt::RPORT", r"Opt::USERNAME", r"Opt::PASSWORD", r"Opt::FILE",
                r"CVE-", r"OpenSSH", r"Debian", r"unauth", r"auth bypass",
                r"version", r"login", r"public.?key"
            ]
            for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
                if len(excerpts) >= 7:
                    break
                if any(re.search(pattern, line, re.I) for pattern in patterns):
                    cleaned = clip(line, 190)
                    key = cleaned.lower()
                    if key not in seen_lines:
                        excerpts.append({"line": lineno, "text": cleaned})
                        seen_lines.add(key)
            result["candidate_files"].append({
                "path": rel,
                "classification": "exploit-path module" if is_exploit else "SSH/OpenSSH source match; review signal present",
                "source_bytes": len(raw),
                "metadata_and_prerequisite_excerpts": excerpts,
                "excerpt_note": "Selected declaration/source lines only; no Ruby parsing or execution."
            })

    result["ssh_path_files"] = len(ssh_paths)
    result["openssh_text_files_outside_ssh_path"] = len(openssh_elsewhere)
    result["read_error_count"] = len(errors)
    result["read_errors"] = errors[:50]
    result["candidate_files"].sort(key=lambda item: item["path"])
    result["candidate_count"] = len(result["candidate_files"])
    result["ssh_path_coverage"] = [rel for rel, _ in ssh_paths]
    result["openssh_text_paths_outside_ssh_path"] = [rel for rel, _ in openssh_elsewhere]
    result["review_scope"] = (
        "All readable Ruby files under the identified modules directory were scanned for SSH/OpenSSH path or text signals; "
        "candidate excerpts are a heuristic subset, not a claim that every module is applicable."
    )

print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True))

nodes.stop_condition: Finish after recording the module-tree inspection coverage and findings, or that the inspection did not provide adequate evidence.

import json
import os
import re

TREE = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules"
SSH_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:open)?ssh\b", re.IGNORECASE)
DETAIL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:Name|Description|Author|References|DisclosureDate|Targets|DefaultOptions|"
    r"register_options|Opt(?:String|Bool|Int|Port|Enum|Address|Raw)|RHOSTS?|RPORT|"
    r"USERNAME|PASSWORD|USER_FILE|PASS_FILE|check|exploit|login|session|auth|"
    r"privileged|rank)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

result = {
    "purpose": "Read-only static review of SSH/OpenSSH-related module source metadata; no modules loaded or executed and no remote requests made.",
    "tree": TREE,
    "tree_exists": os.path.isdir(TREE),
    "coverage": {
        "ruby_files_enumerated": 0,
        "ruby_files_read": 0,
        "ssh_related_files": 0,
        "candidate_files_reported": 0,
        "read_errors": [],
        "scan_scope": "All .rb files reachable by os.walk beneath the located modules tree; candidates are SSH-related files under an exploits path or files whose source mentions OpenSSH."
    },
    "candidates": [],
    "limitations": "Static keyword and source-line review only. Snippets are not executed; source indicators do not prove module applicability, remote vulnerability, or student access."
}

if result["tree_exists"]:
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(TREE, onerror=lambda exc: result["coverage"]["read_errors"].append(str(exc))):
        dirs.sort()
        for name in sorted(files):
            if not name.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            result["coverage"]["ruby_files_enumerated"] += 1
            path = os.path.join(root, name)
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as source_file:
                    lines = source_file.readlines()
                result["coverage"]["ruby_files_read"] += 1
            except OSError as exc:
                result["coverage"]["read_errors"].append({"path": path, "error": str(exc)})
                continue

            path_has_ssh = bool(SSH_RE.search(path))
            matched_lines = [(i + 1, line.rstrip()) for i, line in enumerate(lines) if SSH_RE.search(line)]
            is_ssh_related = path_has_ssh or bool(matched_lines)
            if not is_ssh_related:
                continue
            result["coverage"]["ssh_related_files"] += 1

            relative = os.path.relpath(path, TREE)
            exploit_path = relative.startswith("exploits" + os.sep) or relative.startswith("exploits/")
            openssh_mention = any(re.search(r"open\s*ssh", line, re.IGNORECASE) for _, line in matched_lines)
            if not (exploit_path or openssh_mention):
                continue

            selected = []
            for i, line in enumerate(lines):
                if DETAIL_RE.search(line) or SSH_RE.search(line):
                    text = line.strip()
                    if not text:
                        continue
                    if len(text) > 260:
                        text = text[:257] + "..."
                    selected.append({"line": i + 1, "text": text})
            result["candidates"].append({
                "path": relative,
                "classification_basis": "SSH-related exploit-path source" if exploit_path else "source mentions OpenSSH",
                "metadata_and_prerequisite_source_lines": selected[:18],
                "matching_source_line_count": len(selected)
            })

result["candidates"].sort(key=lambda item: item["path"].lower())
result["coverage"]["candidate_files_reported"] = len(result["candidates"])
print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True))

import json
import os
import re

TREE = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules"

# Selection is deliberately limited to possible SSH access exploits, not SSH
# scanners, fuzzers, DoS modules, or post modules merely mentioning SSH.
OPENSSH_RE = re.compile(r"openssh", re.IGNORECASE)
EVIDENCE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(name|description|references|disclosuredate|rank|targets?|platform|"
    r"check|check_host|exploit|register_options|rport|username|password|"
    r"auth(?:entication|orization)?|login|private.?key|public.?key|version|"
    r"session|privilege|requires?|vuln)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
DESCRIPTION_RE = re.compile(r"['\"]Description['\"]\s*=>")

result = {
    "purpose": "Read-only static source review; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
    "tree": TREE,
    "selection_basis": (
        "Readable Ruby files under exploit/ whose relative path contains an SSH component/name, "
        "or whose source mentions OpenSSH. This selects plausible exploit candidates for review; "
        "it does not establish applicability to the observed service."
    ),
    "tree_readable": os.path.isdir(TREE),
    "ruby_files_discovered": 0,
    "candidate_files_selected": 0,
    "candidates": [],
    "read_errors": [],
    "walk_errors": [],
    "limitations": (
        "Text excerpts are static source evidence, not a Ruby parse. Conditional behavior may "
        "require full source review. No remote service was assessed."
    ),
}

if result["tree_readable"]:
    paths = []

    def on_walk_error(error):
        result["walk_errors"].append({"path": getattr(error, "filename", None), "error": str(error)})

    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(TREE, onerror=on_walk_error):
        dirs.sort()
        for filename in sorted(files):
            if filename.endswith(".rb"):
                paths.append(os.path.join(root, filename))

    result["ruby_files_discovered"] = len(paths)
    candidates = []
    for full_path in paths:
        relative = os.path.relpath(full_path, TREE).replace(os.sep, "/")
        if not relative.startswith("exploit/"):
            continue
        path_has_ssh = bool(re.search(r"(^|[/_-])ssh([/_-]|$)", relative, re.IGNORECASE))
        try:
            with open(full_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as source_file:
                lines = source_file.read().splitlines()
        except OSError as error:
            result["read_errors"].append({"path": relative, "error": str(error)})
            continue

        text = "\n".join(lines)
        mentions_openssh = bool(OPENSSH_RE.search(text))
        if not (path_has_ssh or mentions_openssh):
            continue

        metadata = []
        description_excerpt = []
        in_description = False
        description_lines = 0
        for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            if re.search(r"['\"](?:Name|DisclosureDate|Rank|References|Targets|Platform)['\"]\s*=>", line):
                metadata.append({"line": number, "text": line.strip()[:500]})

        for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):

                    evidence.append({"line": number, "text": item[1]})

        })

    result["candidate_files_selected"] = len(candidates)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import re

TREE = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules"
PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[/_-])(?:ssh|openssh)(?:$|[/_-])", re.I)
SOURCE_RE = re.compile(
    r"open\s*ssh|\bssh\b|rex::proto::ssh|net::ssh|ssh_version|ssh_version|"
    r"ssh[_:]?(?:client|server|login|auth|key|fingerprint|banner|version)",
    re.I,
)
# These lines commonly document module identity, applicability, and access prerequisites.
DETAIL_RE = re.compile(
    r"module_info|['\"](?:name|description|references|targets|platform|arch|rank|"
    r"privileged|actions|defaultoptions)['\"]|\b(?:name|description|references|"
    r"targets|platform|arch|rank|privileged|actions|defaultoptions)\s*=>|"
    r"register_options|\b(?:OptString|OptBool|OptInt|OptEnum|OptPath)\b|"
    r"username|password|private.?key|public.?key|credential|authenticat|"
    r"unauth|login|check\s*\{|check\s*\(|\bssh\b|openssh|"
    r"RHOSTS|RPORT|port\s*=>",
    re.I,
)


def main():
    report = {
        "purpose": "Read-only static source review; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
        "tree": TREE,
        "tree_readable": os.path.isdir(TREE) and os.access(TREE, os.R_OK),
        "ruby_files_discovered": 0,
        "path_signal_files": 0,
        "source_signal_files": 0,
        "candidate_files_selected": 0,
        "candidates": [],
        "walk_errors": [],
        "read_errors": [],
        "limitations": "Text and line matches are static source evidence, not a Ruby parse. Conditional behavior may require full source review; source metadata does not establish remote applicability or vulnerability.",
    }
    if not report["tree_readable"]:
        report["limitations"] += " The located module tree is absent or not readable, so candidate review could not be performed."
        print(json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True))
        return

    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(TREE, onerror=lambda e: report["walk_errors"].append(str(e))):
        dirs.sort()
        for name in sorted(files):
            if not name.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            report["ruby_files_discovered"] += 1
            path = os.path.join(root, name)
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, TREE).replace(os.sep, "/")
            path_signal = bool(PATH_RE.search(rel))
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                    lines = f.readlines()
            except OSError as e:
                report["read_errors"].append({"path": rel, "error": str(e)})
                continue

            hits = [(i + 1, line.rstrip("\r\n")) for i, line in enumerate(lines) if SOURCE_RE.search(line)]
            if path_signal:
                report["path_signal_files"] += 1
            if hits:
                report["source_signal_files"] += 1
            if not path_signal and not hits:
                continue

            detail_lines = [(i + 1, line.rstrip("\r\n")) for i, line in enumerate(lines) if DETAIL_RE.search(line)]
            report["candidates"].append({
                "path": rel,
                "selection_basis": {
                    "ssh_or_openssh_in_relative_path": path_signal,
                    "ssh_or_openssh_source_line_numbers": [n for n, _ in hits],
                },
                "source_line_count": len(lines),
                "metadata_and_prerequisite_lines": [
                    {"line": n, "text": text} for n, text in detail_lines
                ],
                "ssh_source_lines": [
                    {"line": n, "text": text} for n, text in hits
                ],
            })

    report["candidates"].sort(key=lambda item: item["path"].lower())
    report["candidate_files_selected"] = len(report["candidates"])
    report["coverage"] = (
        "Recursive walk of .rb files under the located modules tree; candidate selection includes "
        "SSH/OpenSSH path signals or SSH/OpenSSH source-line signals across all module categories, "
        "not only exploit/. Walk and read errors are listed separately."
    )
    print(json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

nodes.success_criteria: Record the candidate selection basis, relevant tree coverage, and source-backed applicability and prerequisites for each plausible candidate. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only inventory of SSH/OpenSSH-related Metasploit Ruby source."""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

TREE = Path("/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules")
SOURCE_SIGNAL = re.compile(r"\bOpenSSH\b", re.IGNORECASE)
ACCESS_SIGNAL = re.compile(
    r"ssh_login|login|auth|credential|password|public.?key|private.?key|"
    r"unauth|command|shell|exec|session|exploit|vulnerab|bypass",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
DETAIL_SIGNAL = re.compile(
    r"Name|Description|register_options|Opt::|RHOST|RPORT|USER|PASS|KEY|"
    r"Targets|Platform|Arch|Rank|Notes|DisclosureDate|References|check|"
    r"login|auth|unauth|session|exploit|vulnerab|OpenSSH|ssh",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def main():
    result = {
        "purpose": "Read-only static source inventory; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
        "tree": str(TREE),
        "tree_readable": TREE.is_dir() and __import__("os").access(TREE, __import__("os").R_OK),
        "selection_basis": "All readable .rb files under the module tree whose relative path contains 'ssh' (case-insensitive) or whose source contains 'OpenSSH'. This includes exploit and non-exploit directories; it is a broad review set, not proof of applicability.",
        "observed_service_context": "Task-supplied OpenSSH 9.2p1 Debian at 192.168.1.0:22; no remote assessment is performed.",
        "ruby_files_discovered": 0,
        "candidate_files_selected": 0,
        "plausible_access_candidates": 0,
        "files": [],
        "walk_errors": [],
        "read_errors": [],
        "limitations": "Heuristic inventory and source excerpts are not a Ruby parse. Review full source for conditional behavior and complete prerequisites. Static metadata does not establish remote vulnerability or access.",
    }
    if not result["tree_readable"]:
        result["walk_errors"].append("Module tree is absent or not readable: " + str(TREE))
        print(json.dumps(result, separators=(",", ":")))
        return

    paths = []
    try:
        for path in TREE.rglob("*.rb"):
            result["ruby_files_discovered"] += 1
            paths.append(path)
    except OSError as exc:
        result["walk_errors"].append(str(exc))

    for path in sorted(paths):
        rel = path.relative_to(TREE).as_posix()
        path_signal = "ssh" in rel.lower()
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except OSError as exc:
            if path_signal:
                result["read_errors"].append({"path": rel, "error": str(exc)})
            continue
        source_signal = bool(SOURCE_SIGNAL.search(text))
        if not (path_signal or source_signal):
            continue
        result["candidate_files_selected"] += 1
        lines = text.splitlines()
        area = rel.split("/", 1)[0]
        access_related = bool(ACCESS_SIGNAL.search(text))
        plausible = (area == "exploit" and (path_signal or source_signal)) or (
            area == "auxiliary" and path_signal and access_related
        )
        if plausible:
            result["plausible_access_candidates"] += 1

        record = {
            "path": rel,
            "signals": [x for x, yes in (("SSH in path", path_signal), ("OpenSSH in source", source_signal)) if yes],
            "area": area,
            "plausible_access_candidate_heuristic": plausible,
        }
        if plausible:
            record["selection_note"] = "Selected for source review based on exploit-area SSH/OpenSSH identity or auxiliary SSH identity plus access-related source terms; this is a review heuristic, not an applicability conclusion."
            matches = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if DETAIL_SIGNAL.search(line)]
            # Include nearby lines to retain short multi-line metadata and option declarations.
            chosen = set()
            for i in matches:
                chosen.add(i)
                if i > 0 and re.search(r"Description|Name|register_options|Opt::", lines[i - 1], re.I):
                    chosen.add(i - 1)
            excerpts = []
            for i in sorted(chosen):
                line = lines[i].strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                if len(line) > 360:
                    line = line[:357] + "..."
                excerpts.append({"line": i + 1, "source": line})
                if len(excerpts) >= 24:
                    break
            record["source_excerpts"] = excerpts
        else:
            record["selection_note"] = "Included in the broad coverage inventory; not promoted by the access-candidate heuristic."
        result["files"].append(record)

    print(json.dumps(result, separators=(",", ":")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json
import os
import re

ROOT = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules"

# Signals that a module concerns SSH, including protocol use when its path does
# not contain "ssh". Selection is intentionally not restricted to exploit/.
SSH_SIGNAL = re.compile(
    r"(?:\bssh\b|openssh|Rex::Proto::SSH|Net::SSH|ssh_login|ssh_command)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
ACCESS_SIGNAL = re.compile(
    r"(?:unauth|exploit|vulnerab|\bauth(?:entication|orization)?\b|"
    r"credential|user(?:name)?|password|private.?key|public.?key|"
    r"login|session|shell|command|execute|CVE[-_ ]?\d)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
META = re.compile(
    r"\b(Name|Description|DisclosureDate|Rank|License|Targets|Platform|"
    r"Arch|Privileged|DefaultOptions|References|DefaultTarget)\b\s*(?:=>|=|\()"
)
PREREQ = re.compile(
    r"unauth|auth|credential|username|password|private.?key|public.?key|"
    r"USER|PASS|KEY|RHOSTS|RPORT|check\b|login|session|shell|command|"
    r"fail_with|fail\s*\(|CVE[-_ ]?\d",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def excerpt(line, limit=240):
    value = " ".join(line.strip().split())
    return value if len(value) <= limit else value[: limit - 3] + "..."


def module_type(relpath):
    parts = relpath.split(os.sep)
    return parts[0] if parts else "unknown"


def main():
    result = {
        "purpose": "Read-only static source review; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
        "tree": ROOT,
        "tree_readable": os.path.isdir(ROOT) and os.access(ROOT, os.R_OK),
        "selection_basis": (
            "Scan Ruby files throughout the module tree, not just exploit/. Mark SSH signals "
            "from SSH/OpenSSH path components or source references to SSH/OpenSSH libraries "
            "and protocol methods. Review as plausible access candidates those signal files "
            "whose path or source also indicates exploitation, authentication, credentials, "
            "login, execution, sessions, shells, or vulnerability identifiers. This is a "
            "candidate heuristic, not a finding of applicability."
        ),
        "ruby_files_discovered": 0,
        "ssh_signal_files": 0,
        "plausible_candidate_count": 0,
        "ssh_signal_counts_by_module_type": {},
        "candidate_counts_by_module_type": {},
        "candidates": [],
        "walk_errors": [],
        "read_errors": [],
        "limitations": (
            "Excerpts are static text, not a Ruby parse; conditional behavior and complete "
            "prerequisites may require full-source review. Source metadata does not establish "
            "remote vulnerability or access."
        ),
    }
    if not result["tree_readable"]:
        result["limitations"] += " The located module tree is not readable or is absent."
        print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
        return

    for current, dirs, files in os.walk(ROOT, onerror=lambda e: result["walk_errors"].append(str(e))):
        dirs.sort()
        for name in sorted(files):
            if not name.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            result["ruby_files_discovered"] += 1
            path = os.path.join(current, name)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
                    lines = stream.readlines()
            except OSError as exc:
                result["read_errors"].append({"path": relpath, "error": str(exc)})
                continue

            text = "".join(lines)
            path_signal = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[/\\])(?:ssh|openssh)(?:[/\\]|$)", relpath, re.I)) or bool(
                re.search(r"ssh|openssh", relpath, re.I)
            )
            if not path_signal and not SSH_SIGNAL.search(text):
                continue

            kind = module_type(relpath)
            result["ssh_signal_files"] += 1
            result["ssh_signal_counts_by_module_type"][kind] = (
                result["ssh_signal_counts_by_module_type"].get(kind, 0) + 1
            )
            if not (ACCESS_SIGNAL.search(relpath) or ACCESS_SIGNAL.search(text)):
                continue

            result["plausible_candidate_count"] += 1
            result["candidate_counts_by_module_type"][kind] = (
                result["candidate_counts_by_module_type"].get(kind, 0) + 1
            )

            metadata = []
            prereq_lines = []
            for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
                if META.search(line) and len(metadata) < 8:
                    metadata.append({"line": number, "text": excerpt(line)})
                if PREREQ.search(line) and len(prereq_lines) < 10:
                    prereq_lines.append({"line": number, "text": excerpt(line)})

            result["candidates"].append({
                "path": relpath,
                "module_type": kind,
                "selection_signals": {
                    "ssh_in_path": path_signal,
                    "access_related_source_or_path": True,
                },
                "source_metadata_lines": metadata,
                "access_and_prerequisite_lines": prereq_lines,
                "source_line_count": len(lines),
            })

    result["candidates"].sort(key=lambda item: item["path"].lower())
    result["walk_errors"].sort()
    result["read_errors"].sort(key=lambda item: item["path"].lower())
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only static review of SSH/OpenSSH-signal Metasploit exploit sources."""
import json
import os
import re

ROOT = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules/exploits"
SIGNAL = re.compile(r"ssh|openssh", re.I)
INTERESTING = re.compile(
    r"Name\s*=>|Description\s*=>|CVE[-_ ]?\d|OpenSSH|Debian|"
    r"register_options|Opt(?:String|Bool|Int|Port|Enum|Path)|"
    r"USERNAME|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|KEY_PATH|credential|authenticated|"
    r"unauthenticated|pre.?auth|userauth|session|check\b|def exploit|"
    r"def check|login|auth(?:entication)?|targets?\s*=>|References\s*=>|"
    r"Privileged\s*=>|Rank\s*=",
    re.I,
)


def clipped(text, limit=220):
    text = text.strip()
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit - 3] + "..."


def main():
    report = {
        "purpose": "Read-only static source review; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
        "tree": ROOT,
        "coverage": {"walk_completed": False, "ruby_files_examined": 0,
                     "ssh_signal_files_reviewed": 0},
        "review_method": (
            "Walk the exploit subtree, read Ruby files, and select files with SSH/OpenSSH "
            "in the path or source. Excerpts are source evidence, not a Ruby parse or a "
            "finding that the target is vulnerable."
        ),
        "classification_note": (
            "Prerequisite indicators are literal source matches. Absence of a matched "
            "indicator is unknown, not evidence that a prerequisite is absent. Review "
            "the cited source before drawing applicability conclusions."
        ),
        "files": [],
        "walk_errors": [],
        "read_errors": [],
    }
    if not os.path.isdir(ROOT):
        report["limitation"] = "The previously located exploit-tree path is not readable as a directory at execution time."
        print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
        return

    try:
        for directory, dirs, names in os.walk(ROOT, onerror=lambda e: report["walk_errors"].append(str(e))):
            dirs.sort()
            for name in sorted(names):
                if not name.endswith(".rb"):
                    continue
                path = os.path.join(directory, name)
                try:
                    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
                        lines = handle.readlines()
                except OSError as exc:
                    report["read_errors"].append({"path": os.path.relpath(path, ROOT), "error": str(exc)})
                    continue
                report["coverage"]["ruby_files_examined"] += 1
                relpath = os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)
                signal_lines = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if SIGNAL.search(line)]
                path_signal = bool(SIGNAL.search(relpath))
                if not path_signal and not signal_lines:
                    continue

                report["coverage"]["ssh_signal_files_reviewed"] += 1
                selected = set()
                # Include module identity/description, references, options and code-level
                # access/session/exploit clues, with neighboring lines for context.
                for i, line in enumerate(lines):
                    if INTERESTING.search(line):
                        selected.add(i)
                        if re.search(r"Description\s*=>|register_options|Opt(?:String|Bool|Int|Port|Enum|Path)", line, re.I):
                            if i + 1 < len(lines):
                                selected.add(i + 1)
                # Ensure SSH/OpenSSH references are present even if they do not match
                # another metadata pattern.
                selected.update(signal_lines[:4])
                ordered = sorted(selected)
                if len(ordered) > 14:
                    # Retain early metadata and a spread of later code-level evidence.
                    ordered = ordered[:9] + ordered[-5:]
                excerpts = [{"line": i + 1, "text": clipped(lines[i])} for i in ordered]

                lowered = "\n".join(lines).lower()
                indicators = []
                if re.search(r"unauthenticated|without authentication|pre[- ]?auth", lowered):
                    indicators.append("source explicitly mentions unauthenticated/pre-auth behavior")
                if re.search(r"opt\w+\.new\s*\(\s*['\"](?:username|user|password|pass|private_key|key_path)", lowered):
                    indicators.append("source registers an apparent credential/key option")
                if re.search(r"sessiontypes|session\s*=|session\.|session_id|requires?\s+.*session", lowered):
                    indicators.append("source contains a session-related indicator; inspect whether an existing session is required")
                if re.search(r"auth(?:entication)?", lowered) or re.search(r"userauth", lowered):
                    indicators.append("source contains authentication-related code or text")
                if not indicators:
                    indicators.append("no credential/session/access prerequisite classified by these literal indicators")

                report["files"].append({
                    "path": relpath,
                    "source_line_count": len(lines),
                    "selection_signals": {"ssh_in_path": path_signal, "ssh_or_openssh_in_source": bool(signal_lines)},
                    "static_prerequisite_indicators": indicators,
                    "source_excerpts": excerpts,
                    "excerpt_note": "Selected lines are concise source evidence, not complete source or parsed behavior.",
                })
        report["coverage"]["walk_completed"] = not report["walk_errors"]
    except OSError as exc:
        report["walk_errors"].append(str(exc))

    report["coverage"]["candidate_file_count"] = len(report["files"])
    report["limitations"] = []
    if report["walk_errors"]:
        report["limitations"].append("One or more directories could not be fully walked; coverage is incomplete.")
    if report["read_errors"]:
        report["limitations"].append("One or more Ruby files could not be read; review coverage is incomplete.")
    if not report["limitations"]:
        report["limitations"].append(
            "Static excerpts do not establish full conditional behavior, target-version applicability, "
            "remote vulnerability, or a working unauthenticated initial-access path."
        )
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only static review of SSH/OpenSSH-signal Metasploit exploit sources."""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path('/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules/exploits')
SSH_SIGNAL = re.compile(r'(?i)(?:\bssh\b|openssh|sshd|net::ssh|libssh)')
REMOTE = re.compile(r'(?i)\b(?:RHOSTS?|RPORT|connect\s*\(|sock\.put|tcp_socket|peerhost)\b')
EXPLOIT = re.compile(r'(?i)\bdef\s+exploit\b|\bexploit\s*\(')
AUTH = re.compile(r'(?i)(?:USERNAME|USER(?:NAME)?|PASSWORD|PASS(?:WORD)?|PRIVATE_KEY|SSH_KEY|KEY_FILE|USERPASS_FILE|credential|authentication required|authenticated user)')
SESSION = re.compile(r'(?i)SessionTypes|session\s*required|session\.platform|session\.shell_command_token')
KEY_LINE = re.compile(r'(?i)(?:Name|Description|CVE-|References|RHOSTS?|RPORT|USERNAME|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|SSH_KEY|SessionTypes|authenticat|credential|unauth|login|def exploit|def check|OpenSSH|Net::SSH|ssh_)')

def clip(text, limit=190):
    text = ' '.join(text.strip().split())
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit - 3] + '...'

def line_evidence(lines, regex, limit):
    found = []
    for n, text in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if regex.search(text):
            item = {'line': n, 'text': clip(text)}
            if item not in found:
                found.append(item)
            if len(found) >= limit:
                break
    return found

def main():
    if not ROOT.is_dir():
        print(json.dumps({'tree': str(ROOT), 'tree_readable': False,
                          'limitation': 'Located exploits directory is absent or unreadable; no source review performed.'}, indent=2))
        return

    files = []
    walk_errors = []
    read_errors = []
    for base, dirs, names in __import__('os').walk(ROOT, onerror=lambda e: walk_errors.append(str(e))):
        dirs.sort()
        for name in sorted(names):
            if name.endswith('.rb'):
                files.append(Path(base) / name)

    examined = 0
    signal_records = []
    for path in files:
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
        except OSError as exc:
            read_errors.append({'path': str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'error': str(exc)})
            continue
        examined += 1
        lines = text.splitlines()
        rel = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
        path_signal = bool(re.search(r'(?i)(?:^|/)ssh(?:/|_|\.)', rel) or 'openssh' in rel.lower())
        text_signal = bool(SSH_SIGNAL.search(text))
        if not (path_signal or text_signal):
            continue

        remote_evidence = line_evidence(lines, REMOTE, 3)
        exploit_evidence = line_evidence(lines, EXPLOIT, 2)
        is_remote_candidate = bool(remote_evidence and exploit_evidence)
        auth_lines = line_evidence(lines, AUTH, 5)
        session_lines = line_evidence(lines, SESSION, 3)
        # Only call a prerequisite required when the source explicitly marks an
        # option mandatory, or explicitly describes authentication/session need.
        required_auth = []
        for ev in auth_lines:
            source = lines[ev['line'] - 1]
            if re.search(r"\[\s*true\s*,|required|provided credentials|authenticated", source, re.I):
                required_auth.append(ev)
        if not is_remote_candidate:
            if session_lines:
                reason = 'Session-oriented source; no paired remote-target and exploit-method evidence found.'
            elif not remote_evidence:
                reason = 'SSH signal is present, but reviewed source has no matching remote-target evidence.'
            else:
                reason = 'Remote-target text is present, but no matching exploit-method evidence was found.'
            evidence = line_evidence(lines, re.compile(r'(?i)(?:SSH|OpenSSH|SessionTypes|RHOSTS?|RPORT|client|server)'), 2)
            record = {'path': rel, 'classification': 'not_plausible_remote_initial_access_by_review_heuristic',
                      'basis': reason, 'source_evidence': evidence}
        else:
            if session_lines:
                classification = 'requires_or_targets_session_condition'
            elif required_auth:
                classification = 'source_indicates_authentication_or_credential_prerequisite'
            else:
                classification = 'potential_remote_initial_access_candidate_no_explicit_required_credentials_found'
            # Prefer module metadata and prerequisite/behavior lines; retain
            # line numbers so the reader can verify the static source evidence.
            preferred = re.compile(r'(?i)(?:Name|Description|CVE-|References|RHOSTS?|RPORT|USERNAME|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|SSH_KEY|SessionTypes|authenticat|credential|unauth|login|def exploit|def check|OpenSSH|Net::SSH|ssh_)')
            excerpts = line_evidence(lines, preferred, 6)
            record = {'path': rel, 'classification': classification,
                      'source_evidence': excerpts,
                      'remote_target_evidence': remote_evidence,
                      'credential_prerequisite_evidence': required_auth,
                      'session_condition_evidence': session_lines}
        signal_records.append(record)

    candidates = [r for r in signal_records if r['classification'] != 'not_plausible_remote_initial_access_by_review_heuristic']
    noncandidates = [r for r in signal_records if r['classification'] == 'not_plausible_remote_initial_access_by_review_heuristic']
    result = {
        'purpose': 'Static, read-only Ruby source review; modules were not loaded or executed and no remote service was assessed.',
        'tree': str(ROOT), 'tree_readable': True,
        'coverage': {'ruby_files_discovered': len(files), 'ruby_files_read': examined,
                     'ssh_signal_files_reviewed': len(signal_records),
                     'remote_candidate_files': len(candidates),
                     'not_plausible_by_review_heuristic': len(noncandidates)},
        'candidates': candidates,
        'reviewed_signal_files_not_plausible_by_heuristic': noncandidates,
        'walk_errors': walk_errors, 'read_errors': read_errors,
        'limitations': [
            'Classification is a source-review heuristic; Ruby source is not parsed or executed.',
            'A candidate classification is not proof of applicability to OpenSSH 9.2p1 Debian, a vulnerability, unauthenticated access, or a working exploit.',
            'Absence of a detected required-credential line is not proof that no prerequisite exists; consult the cited source lines and full source as needed.'
        ]
    }
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only static review of SSH-signal Ruby files in Metasploit exploits."""
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

TREE = Path('/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules/exploits')
SIGNAL = re.compile(r'\b(?:ssh|openssh)\b|net::ssh|ssh_msg_', re.I)
CANDIDATE_HINT = re.compile(
    r'auth|credential|login|remote|session|shell|command|exec|vuln|cve[-_ ]?\d', re.I
)
IMPORTANT = re.compile(
    r"\b(Name|Description|Rank|DisclosureDate|Privileged|SessionTypes|Targets|"
    r"Notes|Arch|Platform)\b|Opt(?:String|Bool|Int|Port|Address|Path)|"
    r"(?:USERNAME|PASSWORD|PASSWD|PRIVATE.?KEY|SSH.?KEY|AUTH|LOGIN|RHOST|RPORT)|"
    r"check\b|target|credential|authentication|unauthenticated|session|shell|"
    r"command|execute|CVE[-_ ]?\d",
    re.I,
)
CRED = re.compile(r'password|passwd|private.?key|credential|username|user(name)?|auth', re.I)
SESSION = re.compile(r'SessionTypes|session|meterpreter|shell', re.I)


def short(text, limit=170):
    text = ' '.join(text.strip().split())
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[: limit - 3] + '...'


def main():
    result = {
        'purpose': 'Static, read-only source review. No modules loaded or executed; no remote requests.',
        'tree': str(TREE),
        'tree_readable': TREE.is_dir(),
        'ruby_files_discovered': 0,
        'ssh_signal_files': 0,
        'heuristic_candidates': [],
        'other_ssh_signal_files': [],
        'walk_errors': [],
        'read_errors': [],
        'selection_basis': (
            'SSH signal means an SSH/OpenSSH path component or a source reference to SSH/OpenSSH. '
            'A candidate is an SSH-signal file whose path or source also contains authentication, '
            'credential, login, remote, session, shell, command/execution, vulnerability, or CVE '
            'indicators. This is a triage heuristic, not a semantic Ruby analysis.'
        ),
        'limitations': (
            'Selected lines are excerpts, not complete control-flow or prerequisite analysis. '
            'Absence of a credential indicator is not proof that authentication is unnecessary. '
            'Do not infer product/version applicability, a vulnerability, or unauthenticated access '
            'to the observed service from this static review.'
        ),
    }
    if not TREE.is_dir():
        result['limitation'] = 'The expected exploit-tree directory is absent or not readable as a directory.'
        print(json.dumps(result, separators=(',', ':')))
        return

    files = []
    try:
        for path in TREE.rglob('*.rb'):
            files.append(path)
    except OSError as exc:
        result['walk_errors'].append(str(exc))
    files.sort()
    result['ruby_files_discovered'] = len(files)

    for path in files:
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
        except OSError as exc:
            result['read_errors'].append({'path': str(path.relative_to(TREE)), 'error': str(exc)})
            continue
        rel = path.relative_to(TREE).as_posix()
        lines = text.splitlines()
        path_signal = bool(re.search(r'(^|/)(?:ssh|openssh)(/|_|\.)', rel, re.I))
        source_signal = bool(SIGNAL.search(text))
        if not (path_signal or source_signal):
            continue
        result['ssh_signal_files'] += 1
        candidate = bool(CANDIDATE_HINT.search(rel) or CANDIDATE_HINT.search(text))

        # Keep a small, source-backed excerpt set, prioritizing metadata and access conditions.
        selected = []
        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            if IMPORTANT.search(line):
                selected.append((i, short(line)))
        # Preserve order and bound each file's report size.
        evidence = [{'line': n, 'text': s} for n, s in selected[:5]]
        path_parts = rel.lower().split('/')
        post_or_client = any(part in ('post', 'auxiliary') for part in path_parts)
        explicit_credential_lines = [
            {'line': n, 'text': short(line)} for n, line in enumerate(lines, 1)
            if CRED.search(line) and re.search(r'Opt\w+|required|true|SessionTypes|credential|password|private.?key', line, re.I)
        ][:3]
        session_lines = [
            {'line': n, 'text': short(line)} for n, line in enumerate(lines, 1)
            if SESSION.search(line) and re.search(r'SessionTypes|session|meterpreter|shell', line, re.I)
        ][:2]
        if candidate:
            if post_or_client or session_lines:
                access_assessment = 'Source/path suggests a post/session or client-context condition; inspect cited source before treating as initial access.'
            elif explicit_credential_lines:
                access_assessment = 'Credential/authentication-related source indicators found; these may be prerequisites, not proof of unauthenticated access.'
            else:
                access_assessment = 'No explicit credential prerequisite identified by this line scan; this does not establish unauthenticated access.'
            result['heuristic_candidates'].append({
                'path': rel,
                'source_line_count': len(lines),
                'source_evidence': evidence,
                'credential_or_auth_evidence': explicit_credential_lines,
                'session_evidence': session_lines,
                'static_access_observation': access_assessment,
            })
        else:
            result['other_ssh_signal_files'].append({
                'path': rel,
                'source_line_count': len(lines),
                'disposition': 'SSH signal found, but candidate triage indicators were not found in path/source; not classified as a plausible initial-access candidate by the stated heuristic.',
                'source_evidence': evidence[:2],
            })

    result['candidate_count'] = len(result['heuristic_candidates'])
    result['other_signal_file_count'] = len(result['other_ssh_signal_files'])
    result['reviewed_signal_file_count'] = result['candidate_count'] + result['other_signal_file_count']
    print(json.dumps(result, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only static review of SSH/OpenSSH-signal Metasploit exploit sources."""
import json
import os
import re

TREE = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules/exploits"
SIGNAL = re.compile(r"ssh|openssh|sshd|net::ssh|rex::proto::ssh|ssh2", re.I)
DIRECT = re.compile(r"openssh|open.?ssh|ssh server|ssh daemon|sshd|ssh protocol|net::ssh|rex::proto::ssh|ssh_login|ssh connection", re.I)
ACCESS = re.compile(r"username|password|passwd|credential|private.?key|public.?key|authenticat|login|session|meterpreter|shell|targeturi|rhost|rport|check\b|vulnerab|cve[-_ ]?\d", re.I)
META = re.compile(r"\b(Name|Description|Rank|DisclosureDate|Platform|Targets|DefaultTarget|References|SessionTypes|Privileged)\b|Opt(?:String|Bool|Int|Path|Port)\.new", re.I)


def clipped(text, limit=190):
    text = " ".join(text.strip().split())
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit - 1] + "…"


def main():
    report = {
        "purpose": "Read-only static source review; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
        "tree": TREE,
        "tree_readable": os.path.isdir(TREE) and os.access(TREE, os.R_OK),
        "ruby_files_discovered": 0,
        "ssh_signal_files": 0,
        "plausible_direct_ssh_candidates": 0,
        "reviewed_files": [],
        "walk_errors": [],
        "read_errors": [],
        "limitations": "Signal detection and triage are text heuristics. Excerpts are source evidence, not complete control-flow analysis; absence of a credential option does not prove unauthenticated access. No remote service applicability or vulnerability is inferred.",
    }
    if not report["tree_readable"]:
        report["limitations"] += " Exploit tree is unavailable or unreadable at the expected path; no source review was possible."
        print(json.dumps(report, separators=(",", ":")))
        return

    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(TREE, onerror=lambda e: report["walk_errors"].append(str(e))):
        dirs.sort()
        for name in sorted(files):
            if not name.endswith(".rb"):
                continue
            report["ruby_files_discovered"] += 1
            path = os.path.join(root, name)
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, TREE)
            try:
                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as src:
                    lines = src.readlines()
            except OSError as exc:
                report["read_errors"].append({"path": rel, "error": str(exc)})
                continue
            path_signal = bool(SIGNAL.search(rel))
            matching = [(i, line.rstrip("\n")) for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1)
                        if SIGNAL.search(line)]
            if not path_signal and not matching:
                continue
            report["ssh_signal_files"] += 1

            direct_path = bool(DIRECT.search(rel))
            direct_lines = [(i, s) for i, s in matching if DIRECT.search(s)]
            metadata = [(i, s) for i, s in enumerate(lines, 1) if META.search(s)]
            access = [(i, s) for i, s in enumerate(lines, 1) if ACCESS.search(s)]
            is_direct = direct_path or bool(direct_lines)
            # A signal limited to SSH keys, persistence, or a non-SSH transport is
            # recorded but not treated as a direct SSH-service initial-access lead.
            labels = " ".join([rel] + [s for _, s in matching])
            if re.search(r"persistence|ssh.?key|authorized_keys|add.*key", labels, re.I) and not direct_lines:

            # access prerequisites and SSH-specific implementation evidence.
            add(metadata, 2)
            add(access, 4)
            add(direct_lines, 5)
            add(matching, 5)
            chosen.sort(key=lambda x: x["line"])
            entry = {
                "path": rel,
                "source_lines": len(lines),
                "triage": "plausible direct SSH/OpenSSH exploit candidate; applicability requires full source assessment" if is_direct else "SSH signal reviewed; not identified by this static triage as a plausible direct unauthenticated initial-access candidate",
                "evidence": chosen,
            }
            report["reviewed_files"].append(entry)
            if is_direct:
                report["plausible_direct_ssh_candidates"] += 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only lexical review of SSH-related Metasploit exploit Ruby source."""
import json
import os
import re

ROOT = "/usr/share/metasploit-framework/modules/exploits"
SSH_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:ssh|openssh|net::ssh|putty|securecrt)\b", re.I)
HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:Name|Description|Author|References|DisclosureDate|Targets|DefaultTarget)\b")
ROLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"unauthenticated|without authentication|no authentication|pre-auth|preauth|"
    r"username|password|credential|login|auth(?:enticate|entication)?|"
    r"client|SRVPORT|TCPServer|session|meterpreter|post[- ]?auth|"
    r"Net::SSH|ssh_connect|ssh_login|RHOSTS|RPORT",
    re.I,
)


def line_records(text):
    records = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        clean = " ".join(line.strip().split())
        if not clean or clean.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if HEADER_RE.search(clean) or ROLE_RE.search(clean) or SSH_RE.search(clean):
            records.append((number, clean[:220]))
    return records


def classify(records, path):
    joined = "\n".join(text for _, text in records)
    cues = []
    if re.search(r"unauthenticated|without authentication|no authentication|pre[- ]?auth", joined, re.I):
        cues.append("source contains an unauthenticated/pre-auth wording cue; verify its context")
    if re.search(r"Net::SSH|ssh_login|ssh_connect|username|password|credential|login", joined, re.I):
        cues.append("source contains SSH/login or credential-related cues; inspect whether credentials are required")
    if re.search(r"SRVPORT|TCPServer|on_client_connect|client connects|vulnerable client", joined, re.I):
        cues.append("source contains a listener/client-role cue; not necessarily an attack against an SSH server")
    if re.search(r"session|meterpreter|post[- ]?auth", joined, re.I):
        cues.append("source contains session or post-authentication cues")
    if not cues:
        cues.append("no explicit role or access prerequisite cue found in selected source lines")
    return cues


def main():
    result = {
        "purpose": "Static source review only; no module loading, execution, or remote requests.",
        "tree": ROOT,
        "candidate_rule": (
            "A Ruby file is an SSH signal if its relative path or full source contains an SSH/OpenSSH/"
            "Net::SSH/PuTTY/SecureCRT token. It is listed as a candidate only when its path includes an ssh "
            "component or its Name/Description header explicitly names SSH/OpenSSH/PuTTY/SecureCRT. This is "
            "a reproducible lexical triage rule, not proof of exploit applicability."
        ),
        "tree_readable": os.path.isdir(ROOT),
        "ruby_files_discovered": 0,
        "ssh_signal_files": 0,
        "candidate_count": 0,
        "candidates": [],
        "other_ssh_signal_files": [],
        "walk_errors": [],
        "read_errors": [],
        "limitations": (
            "Selected lines and lexical cues are not complete control-flow analysis. A missing credential cue "
            "does not establish unauthenticated access; a candidate label does not establish applicability to "
            "the observed service. Source coverage is limited to files readable during this walk."
        ),
    }
    if not result["tree_readable"]:
        result["error"] = "The located exploit tree is absent or not a directory in this execution environment."
        print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
        return

    paths = []
    for base, dirs, files in os.walk(ROOT, onerror=lambda exc: result["walk_errors"].append(str(exc))):
        dirs.sort()
        for filename in sorted(files):
            if filename.endswith(".rb"):
                paths.append(os.path.join(base, filename))
    result["ruby_files_discovered"] = len(paths)

    for fullpath in paths:
        rel = os.path.relpath(fullpath, ROOT).replace(os.sep, "/")
        try:
            with open(fullpath, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as source_file:
                text = source_file.read()
        except OSError as exc:
            result["read_errors"].append({"path": rel, "error": str(exc)})
            continue
        if not SSH_RE.search(rel) and not SSH_RE.search(text):
            continue
        result["ssh_signal_files"] += 1
        lines = text.splitlines()
        records = line_records(text)
        header_text = "\n".join(line for line in lines[:100] if re.search(r"Name|Description", line, re.I))
        path_ssh = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|/)ssh(?:/|$)", rel, re.I))
        header_ssh = bool(SSH_RE.search(header_text))
        entry = {"path": rel, "source_lines": len(lines)}
        if path_ssh or header_ssh:
            entry["source_cues"] = classify(records, rel)
            # Keep a compact, numbered evidence sample: module identity/description first,
            # then role/prerequisite cues. Every excerpt is an unmodified source line apart
            # from whitespace normalization and length limiting.
            identity = [(n, s) for n, s in records if re.search(r"Name|Description", s, re.I)]
            role = [(n, s) for n, s in records if ROLE_RE.search(s) or SSH_RE.search(s)]
            selected = []
            for item in identity + role:
                if item not in selected:
                    selected.append(item)
                if len(selected) >= 7:
                    break
            entry["evidence"] = [{"line": n, "text": s} for n, s in selected]
            result["candidates"].append(entry)
        else:
            cue = next((s for _, s in records if SSH_RE.search(s)), "SSH token occurs outside candidate path/header")
            entry["triage"] = "SSH signal, but candidate rule not met; no direct SSH identity in path or Name/Description header"
            entry["signal_excerpt"] = cue[:180]
            result["other_ssh_signal_files"].append(entry)

    result["candidate_count"] = len(result["candidates"])
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
